title: Monorepos
definition: A software development strategy where code for many projects is stored in the same repository, as opposed to storing them in separate repositories (polyrepo).
simpleExplanation: Putting your Frontend app, your Backend API, and your Mobile App into one giant Git repository. They share the same `node_modules`, the same ESLint rules, and the same Git history.
realWorldExample: Google famously has the largest Monorepo in the world. Almost all of Google's code (billions of lines) lives in a single repository.
useCases: Easy code sharing between frontend and backend
Atomic commits across entire tech stacks

basic: What is the main problem with Monorepos?
intermediate: What tools are commonly used to manage JavaScript monorepos?

answers.question: Main problem?
answers.answer: Scale. `git clone` becomes incredibly slow if the repository contains 50 different apps and 10 years of history. Git was not originally designed to handle repos with terabytes of data.

answers.question: Management tools?
answers.answer: Tools like Lerna, Nx, Turborepo, and npm/yarn Workspaces.
